scope.reward: one prefunded reward slot and two participant destinations
scope.lean: the actual pure transition functions and guarded adapter commit wrapper, arbitrary natural parameters and finite traces
scope.quint: explicit finite domains in each model, safety only
scope.python: finite implementation tests and differential execution, not formal refinement
scope.adapter: loopback HTTP and SQLite pilot with live credential checks, exact approved proof-export profiles and atomic fixture-credit payout or refund; no production deployment or external financial settlement
scope.adapter_model: two prepared operations, bounded grant/row-version interference, process crashes and lost-response retry; atomic durable commits are modeled, not a SQL implementation-refinement theorem
scope.receipt: unsigned trusted-local execution record, not public verifier authority

assumptions: The caller approves the exact source digest, and the local host is trusted.
Configured IDs stand for authenticated principals and immutable content bindings.
An acceptance trusted flag comes from a controlled verifier; a stop trusted flag comes from an actual stop acknowledgment.
A transition is applied atomically; database linearizability is an integration obligation.
The initial reward slot is already funded, and the configuration is fixed throughout a trace.
Approved proof axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; no other axiom dependencies are permitted.
The correctness of the checkers, host runtimes, OS and compiler used for native execution is outside these service-state proofs.
The adapter trusts its provisioning operator, SQLite, OS and filesystem. Process-crash tests provide local fixture evidence, not a formal storage or external settlement proof.
Controlled checking admits only exact reviewed proof-export profiles. Arbitrary contributor Lean code, public deployment and general proof-worker sandboxing remain outside this pilot.
